description: CHIRPS daily precipitation over South America: the timeline walks the days and the map draws each day's rain, with the curves telling you where to look.
title: Rainfall — CHIRPS over South America · PMTiles, no server

options.content:
# Daily rainfall — the same, with no tile server

This board draws **exactly the same sixty days** as [the original](/d/precip-time), and the difference is in how they reach the screen.

There, each day is a **COG** that a TiTiler cuts into tiles when the map asks for them. Here, each day is a **PMTiles**: one file with the pyramid already drawn inside it, which kepler reads by itself by asking for pieces of the file. The panel's "Raster tile server" option is **deliberately empty** — there is nothing to configure, and that is precisely the case of someone who installs the plugin from Grafana's catalogue and has nowhere to stand a server up.

The price shows in the layer panel: **there is only opacity**. No ramp, no rescaling, no choosing a band — the blue was decided when the file was baked, and there are no numbers underneath left to repaint. In the original those controls are still there.

What each form costs, measured on these same data: a day's COG weighs 631 KB and needs a live server; the archive weighs about 470 KB and needs none.

panels.description: One COG per day. The timeline picks which one is drawn, and the handover between scenes overlaps, so dragging does not flicker.

targets.rawSql:
-- Una fila por día: la fecha, el COG de ese día y las tres cifras que lo
-- resumen. El mismo resultado alimenta el timeline, el mapa y las curvas, así
-- que arrastrar la barra no pide nada al servidor.
SELECT
  dia::TIMESTAMPTZ                    AS time,
  -- El mismo índice, con la URL apuntando al archivo PMTiles en vez de al
  -- COG: mismo día, mismos píxeles, otra forma de servirlos.
  replace(replace(raster_url, '/derived/', 'http://localhost:8089/'), '.tif', '.pmtiles') AS raster_url,
  round(intensidad_mm, 1)             AS intensidad_mm,
  round(fraccion_con_lluvia * 100, 1) AS area_con_lluvia_pct,
  round(max_mm, 0)                    AS max_mm
FROM read_parquet('/derived/chirps-index.parquet')
ORDER BY time

panels.description: Computed on the original floating-point rasters, before quantising: the intensity is the mean of the cells that recorded rain, not of the whole region.
